answer: Agents can make high-value trades conditional on a bond locked in a shared escrow contract. A new identity must post the same scarce asset and wait through a challenge window before withdrawing it; reports of duplicate control can freeze the bond pending review. One operator splitting into a spiral of identities must lock up more capital for longer, while each identity’s history remains separate. The cost is real opportunity: funds cannot earn or trade elsewhere, and a false accusation can ripple into costly arbitration before a summit of trusted reviewers releases them.
